_comment: P2 (G2) SeaweedFS matrix config, TEMPLATE. Rendered at bring-up by the `seaweedfs-iam-init` compose service (docker-compose.yml) into a named volume the `seaweedfs` service mounts read-only — this file itself never carries working credentials or a working STS signing key (see docs/STORAGE-COMPATIBILITY.md's 'Credential hygiene' note: docker-compose.yml doubles as the deployment template, so a committed working key here would have shipped to every deployment, not just local/CI). __SEAWEEDFS_ACCESS_KEY__ / __SEAWEEDFS_SECRET_KEY__ / __SEAWEEDFS_STS_SIGNING_KEY__ are substituted by the init job from SEAWEEDFS_ACCESS_KEY / SEAWEEDFS_SECRET_KEY / SEAWEEDFS_STS_SIGNING_KEY (.env.example) — the signing key is GENERATED per deployment when that var is left unset, never defaulted to a constant. Otherwise mirrors the RustFS-side setup (allow-all role trust) so the storage boundary comparison stays apples-to-apples with RustFS's own well-known defaults plus its 'accept any sts-role-arn string' behavior — not a real IAM identity either way. See docker-compose.yml's `seaweedfs`/`seaweedfs-iam-init` services and docs/STORAGE-COMPATIBILITY.md.
